item.title: Tour guide, tour operator certification classes in February
item.description: (MVA) — In its continuing work to improve visitor satisfaction, the Marianas Visitors Authority — in cooperation with Northern Marianas College — is rebooting its Tour Guide Certification Program with classes in March 2026 and a streamlined process for tour guides and tour operators. item.description: (NMTech) — Northern Marianas Technical Institute, located in Lower Base, is recovering after experiencing flooding that temporarily disrupted campus operations and instructional activities. item.title: 34 residents certified in disaster preparedness by NMC-CREES, DFEMS & HSEM
item.description: (NMC) — Northern Marianas College’s Cooperative Research, Extension, and Education Services- Family, Community, and Youth Development Program, in partnership with the Department of Fire and Emergency Medical Services and CNMI Homeland Security Emergency Management, successfully delivered a series of disaster preparedness and response trainings across the CNMI. item.title: Spending measures for Tinian, Rota OK’d
item.description: Authored by Rep. Patrick San Nicolas, House Local Bill 24-39 appropriating $54,000 in poker fee collections for the Tinian Mayor’s Office, municipal council, and the Tinian Casino Gaming Control Commission is now Tinian Local Law 24-10. The post Spending measures for Tinian, Rota OK’d appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: MVA eyes Philippine market with $500K tourism push
item.description: THE Marianas Visitors Authority board of directors on Wednesday unanimously approved funding of up to $500,000 to issue a request for proposals for Philippines market development, positioning the CNMI to capitalize on the return of direct flights from Manila to Saipan. The post MVA eyes Philippine market with $500K tourism push appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: Judge moves Tinian stablecoin lawsuit forward
item.description: SUPERIOR Court Associate Judge Kenneth L. Govendo has ordered the parties in the Tinian stablecoin lawsuit to submit proposed certified questions by the end of February, tightening the timeline in a case that has been stalled since Attorney General Edward Manibusan moved last year to block the law. The post Judge moves Tinian stablecoin lawsuit forward appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.
